// diagnostic

E0221

A struct field’s strong `Shared` edge can form a reference cycle.

What

A struct field’s strong `Shared` edge can form a reference cycle.

Why

Strong `Shared` handles keep each other alive; a cycle through them never frees.

Fix

use `Shared.Weak<T>` for intentional back-edges, or store an id instead of a strong handle.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0221: tests/ui/shared_strong_cycle.stderr.

Error [E0221]: field `next` on `Node` can form a strong `Shared` cycle
  --> tests/ui/shared_strong_cycle.jet:3:5
    |
  3 |     next: Shared<Node>?
    |     ^^^^
 Why: a strong `Shared` edge through `Node` can point back at `Node`, so reference counting alone cannot free the graph
 Fix: use `Shared.Weak<T>` for intentional back-edges, or store an id instead of a strong `Shared` handle
